title: Migration read
description: One read of an estate at one moment, and the input a verification is built from. It exists as its own contract because the question `what do we need from you` has to have an answer before anybody can be asked for anything: a comparison whose inputs had no shape could not be requested, only improvised. A read states what it found AND what it could not reach, and the second half is what makes it evidence rather than a listing — an inventory that cannot say where it failed to look is indistinguishable from one that looked everywhere.

$schema.description: The exact contract this document claims, which must be the $id of the schema validating it.

read_id.description: How this read is named. Two reads of one estate need distinguishing by more than their order in a command line.

taken_at.description: When the estate was read, which decides which side of the move this is. It is the only field that establishes that a baseline is a baseline.

estate.description: What was read, as the operator named it. Deliberately not a tenant: a move from a file share has no tenant on one side.

produced_by.description: What produced this read. Recorded so a reader can see whether it was the same thing that performed the move.

coverage.description: What this read could NOT establish, and why. An empty array is a claim, not a default: it says the whole declared estate was reached.

items.description: What was found, keyed by the identity used on both sides. An object rather than an array because the identity is the key a comparison joins on, and an array would let one identity appear twice with different attributes.

unsupported.description: Dimensions this source CANNOT provide, ever. Declared by the producer because nothing downstream can infer it: a read with no `author` looks identical whether the surface does not expose authorship or whether this run simply did not ask. Those are different sentences — one is a structural limit of the method, the other is a gap in an execution — and a comparison that renders them the same way manufactures false conclusions the moment a second source appears.

content_digest_algorithm.description: How `content_digest` was computed, for every item this read carries one. Recorded because a digest without its algorithm is not comparable: a quickXorHash and a SHA-256 of the same bytes differ, and a comparison that did not know would report every single item as changed. Present only when the read carries digests at all.

scope.description: What could not be read. Declared over a container, because that is how reading fails: a folder refuses, not a file at a time.

item.description: One item, with whatever this read established about it. Every attribute is optional and absence means the read did not carry it, which a comparison reports as `unknown` rather than treating as equal. A read that omits an attribute for every item is a thinner read than one that carries it, and the comparison says so instead of concluding from silence.

content_digest.description: A digest of the item's content, or null where it was not hashed. Null is deliberate rather than absent: it distinguishes `we chose not to hash` from `this read does not carry digests at all`.

author.description: Who created the item, as the estate reports it. The attribute a move most often rewrites to whatever account performed it, and the loss nobody notices until somebody asks who wrote something.

permissions.description: Principals and roles, as pairs. Sorted by the producer so that two reads of an unchanged item compare equal without the comparison having to know how to order them.
